summary: Compute one shifted natural exponential using four existing PTX instructions and one scratch register.
Derive intermediate finiteness, nonpositivity and all-result accuracy from finite input values and explicit magnitude bounds; return exact positive one when the score equals the supplied maximum.
Prove four fetched steps exist and preserve unrelated state; leave row-maximum computation and parallel softmax separate.

from.quote:
This component computes an approximation to exp(x-m) for one finite stored score
x and a supplied finite upper bound m. The separate parallel maximum component
establishes that property for finite power-of-two rows. Here x and m mean the exact
real values of the input binary32 words, not unrounded external data.

passage.quote:
def InputBounds (x m : ℝ) : Prop :=
  x ≤ m ∧ |x| ≤ (2:ℝ)^(124:ℤ) ∧ |m| ≤ (2:ℝ)^(124:ℤ)

from.quote:
The program uses four already modeled instructions: multiply m by exact minus
one, add that result to x, multiply the shifted result by the encoded approximation
to 1/log(2), then apply ex2.approx.f32. Multiplication by minus one is proved to
negate the finite real value exactly. The addition therefore supplies the rounded
subtraction. This representation reuses the existing addition and multiplication
contracts; it does not claim to formalize sub.rn.f32 or improve performance.

passage.quote:
theorem negative_real (maximum negative : Word) (m : ℝ)
    (value : finiteReal maximum = some m) (small : |m| ≤ (2:ℝ)^(124:ℤ))
    (negate : Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul maximum 0xbf800000 negative) :
    finiteReal negative = some (-m) := by
  have range : |Bounds.exactReal .mul m (-1)| ≤ Bounds.maxFinite := by
    simp only [Bounds.exactReal, mul_neg_one, abs_neg]
    exact small.trans (by rw [Bounds.maxFinite_eq]; norm_num)
  have result := Bounds.round_of_range .mul maximum 0xbf800000 negative m (-1)
    value Bounds.negative_one_real range negate
  change finiteReal negative = some (round32 (m * (-1))) at result
  rw [mul_neg_one] at result
  have fixed : round32 (-m) = -m := by
    change Model.roundAt FloatFormat.binary32 (-m) = -m
    rw [Model.roundAt_neg]
    exact congrArg Neg.neg (round_fixed maximum m value)
  rwa [fixed] at result

from.quote:
The input conditions are x<=m and abs(x),abs(m)<=2^124. These conservative bounds
prevent overflow in the negation, addition and base conversion. The proof derives
that the rounded difference is finite and nonpositive and hence reaches the
supported exponential domain. Finiteness or successful intermediate computations
are conclusions, not extra premises. Both signs of zero and gradual underflow
remain covered by the existing arithmetic contracts.

passage.quote:
theorem shift_real (input maximum negative shifted : Word) (x m : ℝ)
    (inputValue : finiteReal input = some x) (maximumValue : finiteReal maximum = some m)
    (bounds : InputBounds x m)
    (negate : Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul maximum 0xbf800000 negative)
    (shift : Ptx.Binary32.Results .add input negative shifted) :
    finiteReal negative = some (-m) ∧
    finiteReal shifted = some (round32 (x-m)) ∧
    round32 (x-m) ≤ 0 ∧ |round32 (x-m)| ≤ (2:ℝ)^(126:ℤ) ∧
    |round32 (x-m)-(x-m)| ≤ eps32 (x-m) := by
  have negValue := negative_real maximum negative m maximumValue bounds.2.2 negate
  have small : |x-m| ≤ (2:ℝ)^(126:ℤ) := by
    calc
      |x-m| ≤ |x|+|m| := abs_sub x m
      _ ≤ (2:ℝ)^(124:ℤ)+(2:ℝ)^(124:ℤ) := add_le_add bounds.2.1 bounds.2.2
      _ ≤ (2:ℝ)^(126:ℤ) := by norm_num
  have range : |Bounds.exactReal .add x (-m)| ≤ Bounds.maxFinite := by
    change |x + -m| ≤ Bounds.maxFinite
    rw [← sub_eq_add_neg]
    exact small.trans (by rw [Bounds.maxFinite_eq]; norm_num)
  have value := Bounds.round_of_range .add input negative shifted x (-m)
    inputValue negValue range shift
  change finiteReal shifted = some (round32 (x + -m)) at value
  rw [← sub_eq_add_neg] at value
  have nonpos : round32 (x-m) ≤ 0 := by
    have h := Model.roundAt_mono FloatFormat.binary32 (sub_nonpos.mpr bounds.1)
    rwa [Model.roundAt_zero] at h
  have hi := Model.roundAt_mono FloatFormat.binary32 (abs_le.mp small).2
  have lo := Model.roundAt_mono FloatFormat.binary32 (abs_le.mp small).1
  change round32 (x-m) ≤ round32 ((2:ℝ)^(126:ℤ)) at hi
  rw [bound_fixed] at hi
  rw [Model.roundAt_neg] at lo
  change -round32 ((2:ℝ)^(126:ℤ)) ≤ round32 (x-m) at lo
  rw [bound_fixed] at lo
  exact ⟨negValue,value,nonpos,abs_le.mpr ⟨lo,hi⟩,
    TorchLean.Floats.FP32.round_abs_error (x-m)⟩

theorem stages_exist (input maximum : Word) (x m : ℝ)
    (inputValue : finiteReal input = some x) (maximumValue : finiteReal maximum = some m)
    (bounds : InputBounds x m) :
    ∃ negative shifted product output,
      Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul maximum 0xbf800000 negative ∧
      Ptx.Binary32.Results .add input negative shifted ∧
      Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul shifted ExpArgument.constantWord product ∧
      Exponential.Results product output := by
  obtain ⟨negative,negate⟩ := Ptx.Binary32.results_exists .mul maximum 0xbf800000
  obtain ⟨shifted,shift⟩ := Ptx.Binary32.results_exists .add input negative
  have h := shift_real input maximum negative shifted x m inputValue maximumValue bounds negate shift
  obtain ⟨product,multiply⟩ := Ptx.Binary32.results_exists .mul shifted ExpArgument.constantWord
  have productValue := ExpArgument.product_real shifted product _ h.2.1 h.2.2.1
    (ExpArgument.bounded_product_range _ h.2.2.2.1) multiply
  obtain ⟨output,approximate⟩ := Exponential.results_exists product
    (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨_,productValue.1,productValue.2⟩)))
  exact ⟨negative,shifted,product,output,negate,shift,multiply,approximate⟩

from.quote:
Write z=round32(x-m), where round32 rounds to the nearest binary32 grid value,
choosing the value with an even final bit on a tie. The shift error is at most
eps32(x-m), the half-ULP rounding allowance. Every permitted final output is finite
and differs from exp(x-m) by at most
`5*2^-24 + log(2)*ExpArgument.budget(z,eps32(x-m))`.
The total bound includes addition rounding, approximation of 1/log(2), multiplication
rounding and the exponential allowance. When x=m, the final word is exactly positive one, including differently signed
zero inputs. The exponential preserves both named ULP
spacing interpretations; no unique hardware result is selected.

passage.quote:
theorem error (input maximum negative shifted product output : Word) (x m : ℝ)
    (inputValue : finiteReal input = some x) (maximumValue : finiteReal maximum = some m)
    (bounds : InputBounds x m)
    (negate : Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul maximum 0xbf800000 negative)
    (shift : Ptx.Binary32.Results .add input negative shifted)
    (multiply : Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul shifted ExpArgument.constantWord product)
    (approximate : Exponential.Results product output) :
    ∃ z : ℝ, finiteReal output = some z ∧
      |z-Real.exp (x-m)| ≤ 5/(2:ℝ)^24 + Real.log 2 *
        ExpArgument.budget (round32 (x-m)) (eps32 (x-m)) := by
  have h := shift_real input maximum negative shifted x m inputValue maximumValue bounds negate shift
  have range := ExpArgument.bounded_product_range _ h.2.2.2.1
  have productValue := ExpArgument.product_real shifted product _ h.2.1 h.2.2.1 range multiply
  exact ExpArgument.natural_exp_error _ (x-m) _ shifted product output h.2.1 h.2.2.1
    (sub_nonpos.mpr bounds.1) range h.2.2.2.2 multiply
    (Exponential.finiteExp2 product output _ productValue.1 approximate)

theorem equal_scores (input maximum negative shifted product output : Word) (m : ℝ)
    (inputValue : finiteReal input = some m) (maximumValue : finiteReal maximum = some m)
    (small : |m| ≤ (2:ℝ)^(124:ℤ))
    (negate : Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul maximum 0xbf800000 negative)
    (shift : Ptx.Binary32.Results .add input negative shifted)
    (multiply : Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul shifted ExpArgument.constantWord product)
    (approximate : Exponential.Results product output) : output = 0x3f800000 := by
  have h := shift_real input maximum negative shifted m m inputValue maximumValue
    ⟨le_rfl,small,small⟩ negate shift
  have zeroRound : round32 0 = 0 := Model.roundAt_zero FloatFormat.binary32
  have shiftedZero : finiteReal shifted = some 0 := by
    simpa only [sub_self,zeroRound] using h.2.1
  have productValue := ExpArgument.product_real shifted product 0 shiftedZero le_rfl
    (ExpArgument.bounded_product_range 0 (by norm_num)) multiply
  have productZero : finiteReal product = some 0 := by
    simpa only [zero_mul,zeroRound] using productValue.1
  exact (Exponential.zero_iff product output productZero).mp approximate

The instruction sequence uses one destination register as scratch throughout.
It must differ from the score register, which remains live until the addition.
The destination may coincide with the maximum register because the maximum is
read before that register is overwritten. The standalone sequence starts at instruction position zero. Actual instruction
fetch, original-state
operand reads and four steps connect the final destination to the numerical
bound. An execution exists for every admitted initial state on the selected PTX 9.4
target with SM version at least 20, preserving subnormals without flush-to-zero.
Other word registers, predicates, address registers and memory are preserved.

def Run (target : Ptx.Target) (program : List Instr) (s t : Scalar.State) : Prop :=
  ∃ s₁ s₂ s₃ e₀ e₁ e₂ e₃,
    Step target program s s₁ e₀ ∧ Step target program s₁ s₂ e₁ ∧
    Step target program s₂ s₃ e₂ ∧ Step target program s₃ t e₃

theorem run_results (target : Ptx.Target) (s t : Scalar.State)
    (input maximum destination : Nat) (start : s.pc = 0)
    (scratch : destination ≠ input)
    (run : Run target (program input maximum destination) s t) :
    (∃ negative shifted product,
      Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul (s.regs maximum) 0xbf800000 negative ∧
      Ptx.Binary32.Results .add (s.regs input) negative shifted ∧
      Ptx.Binary32.Results .mul shifted Ptx.Binary32.ExpArgument.constantWord product ∧
      Ptx.Binary32.Exponential.Results product (t.regs destination)) ∧
    t.pc = 4 ∧ t.memory = s.memory ∧ t.addrs = s.addrs ∧ t.preds = s.preds ∧
    (∀ other, other ≠ destination → t.regs other = s.regs other) := by
  rcases run with ⟨s₁,s₂,s₃,e₀,e₁,e₂,e₃,h₀,h₁,h₂,h₃⟩
  obtain ⟨a₀,b₀⟩ := binary_of_step (i := negate maximum destination) (by simp [program,start]) h₀
  have f₀ := Scalar.Binary32.eval_frame _ _ _ _ b₀
  have pc₁ : s₁.pc = 1 := by omega
  obtain ⟨a₁,b₁⟩ := binary_of_step (i := shift input destination) (by simp [program,pc₁]) h₁
  have f₁ := Scalar.Binary32.eval_frame _ _ _ _ b₁
  have pc₂ : s₂.pc = 2 := by omega
  obtain ⟨a₂,b₂⟩ := binary_of_step (i := convert destination) (by simp [program,pc₂]) h₂
  have f₂ := Scalar.Binary32.eval_frame _ _ _ _ b₂
  have pc₃ : s₃.pc = 3 := by omega
  obtain ⟨a₃,b₃⟩ := exponential_of_step (i := exponential destination) (by simp [program,pc₃]) h₃
  have f₃ := Scalar.Exponential.eval_frame _ _ _ _ b₃
  have r₀ := Scalar.Binary32.eval_destination _ _ _ _ b₀ (by rfl)
  have r₁ := Scalar.Binary32.eval_destination _ _ _ _ b₁ (by rfl)
  have r₂ := Scalar.Binary32.eval_destination _ _ _ _ b₂ (by rfl)
  have r₃ := Scalar.Exponential.eval_destination _ _ _ _ b₃ (by rfl)
  have saved : s₁.regs input = s.regs input :=
    Scalar.Binary32.eval_other _ _ _ _ input b₀ (Ne.symm scratch)
  simp only [negate,shift,convert,exponential,Scalar.Operand32.eval] at r₀ r₁ r₂ r₃
  rw [saved] at r₁
  refine ⟨⟨s₁.regs destination,s₂.regs destination,s₃.regs destination,r₀,r₁,r₂,r₃⟩,
    by omega, f₃.2.1.trans (f₂.2.1.trans (f₁.2.1.trans f₀.2.1)),
    f₃.2.2.1.trans (f₂.2.2.1.trans (f₁.2.2.1.trans f₀.2.2.1)),
    f₃.2.2.2.trans (f₂.2.2.2.trans (f₁.2.2.2.trans f₀.2.2.2)), ?_⟩
  intro other different
  exact (Scalar.Exponential.eval_other _ _ _ _ other b₃ different).trans
    ((Scalar.Binary32.eval_other _ _ _ _ other b₂ different).trans
      ((Scalar.Binary32.eval_other _ _ _ _ other b₁ different).trans
        (Scalar.Binary32.eval_other _ _ _ _ other b₀ different)))

theorem correct (target : Ptx.Target) (s t : Scalar.State)
    (input maximum destination : Nat) (x m : ℝ)
    (start : s.pc = 0) (scratch : destination ≠ input)
    (inputValue : Ptx.Binary32.finiteReal (s.regs input) = some x)
    (maximumValue : Ptx.Binary32.finiteReal (s.regs maximum) = some m)
    (bounds : Ptx.Binary32.ShiftedExp.InputBounds x m)
    (run : Run target (program input maximum destination) s t) :
    ∃ u, Ptx.Binary32.finiteReal (t.regs destination) = some u ∧
      |u-Real.exp (x-m)| ≤ 5/(2:ℝ)^24 + Real.log 2 *
        Ptx.Binary32.ExpArgument.budget (TorchLean.Floats.round32 (x-m))
          (TorchLean.Floats.eps32 (x-m)) := by
  obtain ⟨⟨negative,shifted,product,r₀,r₁,r₂,r₃⟩,_⟩ :=
    run_results target s t input maximum destination start scratch run
  exact Ptx.Binary32.ShiftedExp.error _ _ negative shifted product _ x m
    inputValue maximumValue bounds r₀ r₁ r₂ r₃

theorem maximal_score (target : Ptx.Target) (s t : Scalar.State)
    (input maximum destination : Nat) (m : ℝ)
    (start : s.pc = 0) (scratch : destination ≠ input)
    (inputValue : Ptx.Binary32.finiteReal (s.regs input) = some m)
    (maximumValue : Ptx.Binary32.finiteReal (s.regs maximum) = some m)
    (small : |m| ≤ (2:ℝ)^(124:ℤ))
    (run : Run target (program input maximum destination) s t) :
    t.regs destination = 0x3f800000 := by
  obtain ⟨⟨negative,shifted,product,r₀,r₁,r₂,r₃⟩,_⟩ :=

  exact Ptx.Binary32.ShiftedExp.equal_scores _ _ negative shifted product _ m
    inputValue maximumValue small r₀ r₁ r₂ r₃

theorem execution_exists (target : Ptx.Target) (s : Scalar.State)
    (input maximum destination : Nat) (x m : ℝ)
    (supported : Scalar.Binary32.SupportedTarget target)
    (start : s.pc = 0) (scratch : destination ≠ input)
    (inputValue : Ptx.Binary32.finiteReal (s.regs input) = some x)
    (maximumValue : Ptx.Binary32.finiteReal (s.regs maximum) = some m)
    (bounds : Ptx.Binary32.ShiftedExp.InputBounds x m) :
    ∃ t, Run target (program input maximum destination) s t := by
  obtain ⟨n,z,a,u,r₀,r₁,r₂,r₃⟩ := Ptx.Binary32.ShiftedExp.stages_exist
    (s.regs input) (s.regs maximum) x m inputValue maximumValue bounds
  let s₁ := write s destination n
  let s₂ := write s₁ destination z
  let s₃ := write s₂ destination a
  let t := write s₃ destination u
  have b₀ : Scalar.Binary32.Eval (negate maximum destination) s s₁
      (Scalar.Binary32.occurrence s (negate maximum destination) true) :=
    .executed rfl r₀
  have b₁ : Scalar.Binary32.Eval (shift input destination) s₁ s₂
      (Scalar.Binary32.occurrence s₁ (shift input destination) true) := by
    apply Scalar.Binary32.Eval.executed rfl
    simpa [s₁,write,shift,Scalar.Operand32.eval,Scalar.update,Ne.symm scratch] using r₁
  have b₂ : Scalar.Binary32.Eval (convert destination) s₂ s₃
      (Scalar.Binary32.occurrence s₂ (convert destination) true) := by
    apply Scalar.Binary32.Eval.executed rfl
    simpa [s₂,write,convert,Scalar.Operand32.eval,Scalar.update] using r₂
  have b₃ : Scalar.Exponential.Eval (exponential destination) s₃ t
      (Scalar.Exponential.occurrence s₃ (exponential destination) true) := by
    apply Scalar.Exponential.Eval.executed rfl
    simpa [s₃,write,exponential,Scalar.Operand32.eval,Scalar.update] using r₃
  refine ⟨t,s₁,s₂,s₃,_,_,_,_,⟨supported,_,?_,.binary b₀⟩,
    ⟨supported,_,?_,.binary b₁⟩,⟨supported,_,?_,.binary b₂⟩,
    ⟨supported,_,?_,.exponential b₃⟩⟩ <;>
    simp [program,s₁,s₂,s₃,write,start]

passage.quote:
The supported input domain consists of finite nonpositive values, both
infinities, and NaN (not a number). Both signs of zero produce exactly positive
one. Negative infinity produces positive zero; positive infinity produces
positive infinity. NaN permits any NaN output in the existing conservative
payload policy. For strictly negative finite inputs, every finite result in the
reviewed two-ULP neighborhood is retained. ULP means the spacing of the floating
point grid: the neighborhood uses the larger spacing at the nearest-even rounded
reference and at the returned value. This covers the two named conventions,
without claiming a unique interpretation of NVIDIA's wording or physical
realizability of every permitted bit pattern.

links.reason: The final fetched instruction must preserve every admitted finite exponential result and enforce the exact signed-zero special case.
